cards.title: Use Reddit comments for sentiment, not citation growth
cards.claim: One speaker reports that Reddit comments have not meaningfully changed discovery direction and views comments primarily as a sentiment signal rather than a way to increase ChatGPT citations.
cards.action: Use comments to assess sentiment; do not rely on repeated commenting to become “on the top” or increase ChatGPT citations.
applies_when: You are already being discovered via Reddit or in ChatGPT.
You are deciding how to use Reddit comments.
do_not_use_when: You need evidence that comments never affect discovery or citations.
You are making a claim about all LLMs or all Reddit posts.
unknowns: How discovery and citations were measured.
Whether effects vary by subreddit, query, account, or LLM.
The scale and duration of the speaker's observations.
evidence_quotes: I haven't seen comments having a meaningful impact act in changing the direction of your discovery.
comments are more for sentiment I would say
if you're thinking that hey I would just keep commenting and I would you know end up being on the top or you know my charge citations would increase I don't think that would work.

cards.title: Niche comparison queries in competitive categories
cards.claim: A speaker recommends starting with narrower category-and-audience queries, such as CRM for healthcare, to reduce competition before pursuing broad category terms.
cards.action: Start with a narrower query such as “best CRM for healthcare” or “best CRM for sales people in health tech” rather than only targeting “best CRM.”
applies_when: You can describe a specific industry or audience segment your product serves.
do_not_use_when: You cannot substantiate that the product fits the niche.
You need proof that niche targeting will produce rankings or topical authority.
unknowns: Whether LLMs use the same ranking signals as SEO.
How much niche specificity is required.
Whether success on niche queries transfers to broad category queries.

cards.title: Monitor citation share because citation lifetime is unknown
cards.claim: The speakers describe citation visibility as an ongoing effort and say they manually track citations and changes in citation share, while acknowledging that citation lifetime is unknown.
cards.action: Track where you are cited and monitor citation share over time, including whether it changes later.
applies_when: You are monitoring LLM citations or discovery visibility over time.
You need a provisional tracking process while citation persistence is uncertain.
do_not_use_when: You need a validated citation half-life.
You want to claim that citations expire after a specific period.
unknowns: The lifetime or “half-life” of a citation.
Whether citation persistence differs by LLM.
Whether a change in citation share reflects ranking, indexing, prompt variation, or another factor.
evidence_quotes: it is ever on running engine you have to keep keep doing it.
I still don't have a formula on you know uh what is the lifetime of a citation
my bigger theory is there is a halfife of citation
we are just manually tracking on a excel sheet you know like this got cited here and then we are trying to look at it citation share and do we see a change in citation share somewhere down the line
